jobs.title: Environmental Scientist, Planning Waters Team Lead
jobs.description:
Grounded in safety, quality, and ethics, our experts lead their fields and guide our work with rigor, a creative spirit, and a vision for growth. We draw from more than 20 technical specialties worldwide and are committed to fostering an inclusive community of diverse talents, backgrounds, and expertise. We’re a place to apply your passion and collaborate with top environmental talents on work critical to our clients and the communities they support. Join a team that has the environment down to a science.

Your Opportunity

Stantec is seeking an experienced Environmental Scientist to serve as a Planning Waters Team Lead for a large utility client within our environmental planning and natural resources practice. This position will provide technical and operational leadership for planning-related waters work, including jurisdictional waters and aquatic resources assessments, regulatory permitting, technical documentation, and environmental review.

The successful candidate will function as an experienced professional who applies advanced practical knowledge, exercises independent judgment, and resolves complex technical and project-delivery issues within established professional and regulatory practices. The role will also provide mentoring, work coordination, quality oversight, and technical direction to environmental scientists and other multidisciplinary team members.

Location

This role is based out of our Stantec office in San Diego, CA; however geographic alignment with other Stantec offices can be considered based on experience. Stantec offers flexible work locations (including working from home), flexible work hours, and a robust compensation and benefits package. Typical office environment working with computers and remaining sedentary for long periods of time.

Your Key Responsibilities

* Provide technical and functional leadership for planning-related waters assignments, including aquatic resource evaluations, jurisdictional waters delineations, desktop assessments, field investigations, permitting, and environmental documentation.
* Coordinate team workloads, assign or recommend assignments based on staff qualifications and availability, monitor schedules and deliverables, and identify resource needs or delivery risks.
* Provide technical direction, coaching, mentoring, and quality-control support to junior and intermediate staff.
* Develop regulatory strategies for projects requiring aquatic resource approvals or consultation.
* Prepare and review permit applications and supporting materials associated with Clean Water Act Sections 404 and 401, Waste Discharge Requirements, and California Fish and Game Code Section 1600 Lake and Streambed Alteration Agreements, as applicable.
* Prepare, review, and provide quality assurance and quality control for jurisdictional waters delineation reports, Aquatic Resources Delineation Reports, technical memoranda, biological resources reports, and permit packages.
* Interpret federal, state, and local environmental requirements and advise project teams on applicable regulatory pathways, risks, data needs, and recommended next steps.
* Coordinate with clients, project managers, technical specialists, and regulatory agencies regarding project requirements, technical findings, schedules, deliverables, and permitting strategies.
* Lead or support agency coordination and negotiations, including responding to agency comments and requests for supplemental information.
* Review work prepared by team members for technical accuracy, consistency, regulatory defensibility, completeness, and adherence to applicable quality standards.
* Develop and improve team procedures, templates, quality-control tools, technical guidance, and training materials to support consistent project delivery.
* Lead by example in applying Stantec and client health, safety, security, and environmental requirements.

Your Capabilities and Credentials

* Advanced practical knowledge of aquatic resources, jurisdictional waters, wetlands, streams, riparian systems, and related environmental planning and permitting requirements.
* Working knowledge of the Clean Water Act, including Sections 404 and 401; applicable state water-quality requirements; Waste Discharge Requirements; and California Fish and Game Code Section 1600 requirements.
* Experience developing aquatic resource permitting strategies and preparing or reviewing permit applications and supporting technical documentation.
* Ability to independently evaluate complex technical and regulatory issues, interpret available information, and recommend practical, defensible solutions.
* Demonstrated ability to lead technical workstreams, coordinate workloads, guide teams, and deliver assignments within established scope, budget, schedule, and quality expectations.
* Experience mentoring staff, reviewing technical work, providing constructive feedback, and supporting employee development.
* Strong technical writing, editing, verbal communication, presentation, and organizational skills.
* Ability to communicate technical information clearly to clients, project managers, multidisciplinary teams, regulatory agencies, and other stakeholders.
* Ability to build productive professional relationships and work collaboratively across offices, disciplines, and business lines.
* Strong attention to detail and commitment to technically accurate, complete, and high-quality deliverables.
* Proficiency with Microsoft Office applications and Adobe Acrobat.
* Must have valid driver's license and clean MVR

Education and Experience

Bachelor’s degree in environmental science, biology, ecology, wetland science, natural resources, soil science, botany, environmental planning, or a related discipline.

Minimum of five years of directly related professional experience, or an equivalent combination of education and experience.

Experience successfully leading the technical aspects of small to medium projects or significant workstreams within larger, m

jobs.title: Environmental Scientist/Project Manager
jobs.description:
Do you like working with different project teams in a fast-paced environment? Are you interested in joining an organization focused on making a positive impact? If so, we'd like to talk with you about growing with us.

EnSafe is seeking a full-time Environmental Scientist/Project Manager to join our team of professionals at our San Diego or Long Beach CA, office.

This position has a requirement to work onsite, at the San Diego or Long Beach, CA office, if needed relocation assistance may be offered to meet this expectation.

**What we are looking for**

An Environmental Scientist with proven experience managing environmental due diligence projects and a strong ability to translate complex findings into clear, defensible Phase I ESA reports. You'll work with clients across California and beyond, managing projects from site assessment through final reporting while gaining exposure to Phase II investigations, environmental sampling, and emerging areas such as PFAS risk evaluation.

Joining our team means immersing yourself in an environment that nurtures creativity, encourages collaboration at all levels, fosters a supportive culture, and facilitates professional development.

***Key responsibilities of this position include***

***What you will be doing:***

* Perform and manage Phase I Environmental Site Assessments in accordance with ASTM and applicable regulatory requirements.
* Conduct site reconnaissance, historical research, regulatory database review, interviews, and other due diligence activities.
* Prepare clear, technically sound Phase I ESA reports and recommendations.
* Manage multiple Phase I ESA projects, including scope, schedule, budget, subcontractors, client communication, and deliverables.
* Provide technical and peer review of Phase I ESA reports as experience permits.
* Support Phase II environmental site investigations and other due diligence activities when warranted.
* Plan and conduct environmental sampling activities involving soil, groundwater, soil vapor, indoor air, surface water, or other environmental media.
* Prepare work plans, technical memoranda, investigation reports, and proposals.
* Communicate findings and environmental risk considerations clearly to clients and project teams.
* Coordinate work with junior staff and provide technical guidance and mentoring.
* Support environmental compliance projects based on experience and workload, which may include hazardous materials and hazardous waste management, SPCC, stormwater, wastewater, EPCRA/Tier II, or related regulatory requirements.
* Participate in business development activities, including preparation of scopes, budgets, proposals, and support for existing client relationships.
* Travel periodically to project sites throughout California and as needed, elsewhere in the United States.

***Minimum Skills and Requirements***

* Bachelor's degree in environmental science, Geology, Environmental Engineering, or a related scientific or engineering discipline.
* Approximately 6 or more years of relevant environmental consulting experience.
* Demonstrated experience preparing Phase I Environmental Site Assessments.
* Strong technical writing and report preparation skills.
* Ability to independently conduct site reconnaissance and evaluate environmental conditions.
* Working knowledge of environmental due diligence practices and applicable federal and state environmental regulations.
* Ability to manage schedules, budgets, client expectations, and multiple concurrent assignments.
* Strong written and verbal communication skills.
* Strong critical-thinking and problem-solving skills.
* Ability and willingness to travel to support project work.
* Valid driver's license and ability to perform field activities associated with environmental site assessments.

***Preferred Qualifications***

***The following experience would be beneficial but is not required:***

* Experience managing Phase I ESA programs or providing technical/peer review.
* Qualification as an Environmental Professional under ASTM/AAI requirements.
* Phase II ESA, subsurface investigation, soil, groundwater, or vapor assessment experience.
* Environmental compliance experience, including hazardous waste, hazardous materials, SPCC, stormwater, wastewater, CERS/HMBP, or EPCRA/Tier II reporting.
* Experience supporting industrial, commercial real estate, logistics/warehouse, energy, municipal, or similar clients.
* Professional Geologist (PG), Professional Engineer (PE), or other relevant professional certification.
* Building sciences or hazardous building materials experience.
* Experience with asbestos-containing materials, lead-based paint, mold/microbial assessments, or related building surveys.
* California asbestos or lead certifications.
* 40-hour HAZWOPER training.

**Why Join EnSafe?**

* **Employee-Owned Advantage**  
  EnSafe is 100% employee-owned, with an ESOP (Employee Stock Ownership Plan) since 1997. That means when EnSafe succeeds, you succeed too, turning company growth directly into shared rewards.
* **Commitment to Growth and Wellness**  
  The company supports personalized career development, mentorship, and employee wellness initiatives such as health tracking tools.
* **Purpose‑Driven Work**  
  EnSafe's mission focuses on impactful environmental, health, and safety consulting—making a real difference in communities and is backed by its long-standing technical credibility.
* **Safety as a Value, Not Just a Service**  
  Safety is deeply embedded in our culture, prioritizing employee well-being in addition to helping clients maintain compliance. We stress that *"safety is part of everything we do."*
* **A Culture of Freedom & Ownership**  
  At EnSafe, our career philosophy is built on freedom. The freedom to take initiative, achieve your goals, and shape your own career path Employees are encouraged to pursue growth in a flexible, entrepreneurial environment.
